name: Electric body groomer
lead: An electric body groomer is a battery or mains-powered trimmer designed for hair on the chest, abdomen, back, arms and groin. It typically combines a protective guard or foil-style blade head with adjustable length settings, so that hair is cut to a chosen length rather than removed or shaved to the skin.

Trimming is classified in the hair-removal literature as a way of shortening hair rather than removing it from the follicle, and the effect lasts only as long as it takes the hair to grow back, generally days. Reviews of hair removal practices divide methods into depilation (removal of the shaft, including shaving and chemical products) and epilation (removal of the shaft and follicle), and state that all methods other than electrolysis are temporary [1].

No clinical trials of electric body groomers as a device category were identified. The evidence relevant to them comes from general reviews of hair removal practices, including a 2023 review of hair removal in the genital area that covers motivation, methods and risks [2].

paras: Body groomers resemble beard trimmers but usually use a wider cutting head with blunted or protected blades and a set of comb guards for different lengths. Models marketed for the groin and torso often add a foil or ceramic-blade head, a waterproof body for use in the shower and a cordless rechargeable motor. Some are sold as attachments to multipurpose grooming kits.

They are related to, but distinct from, electric foil and rotary shavers, which cut hair at or near skin level. Shaving as a whole is described as the removal of hair at the skin surface with a bladed tool, and electric versions are a common alternative to wet shaving [3].

A motor oscillates a blade set behind a guard. The guard holds the skin away from the blades while hairs that protrude through the teeth are cut at a set height. Because the cut occurs above the skin and the follicle is left intact, hair continues its normal growth cycle and re-emerges as ordinary tapered-tip or blunt-tipped hair within days [1].

Trimming achieves a shorter hair length rather than a hairless surface, and the visual result depends on the guard setting. The literature on hair removal compares methods mainly by how long they last and by their adverse effects, with epilation and laser-based methods lasting longer than depilation and cutting [1].
A 2023 review of hair removal in the genital area describes the motives people report for removing hair and discusses the risks of different techniques [2].

Reviews of hair removal describe the main complications of shaving-type methods as nicks and cuts, skin irritation and ingrown hairs [1][3]. Because a body groomer's guard keeps the cutting edge away from the skin, proponents regard it as a lower-contact option, though no studies directly compare the complication rates of guarded trimmers and razors.

In the genital area, a review of epilation and depilation practices discusses injuries and infections associated with hair removal as a group and highlights hygiene as a factor [2]. Manufacturers' instructions generally advise cleaning and drying the blades after use.

In grooming discussions, body groomers are generally presented as the option for people who want to reduce body hair while keeping a natural look, as opposed to a fully smooth result from shaving, waxing or laser. Typical subjects are chest and abdominal hair, back hair and pubic grooming. The site's own rating treats a body groomer as a low-cost, short-lived option with a minimal risk profile.
No studies found. General reviews of hair removal practices, which describe cutting and shaving among temporary methods, are the closest available literature [1][2].
